title: Review Policy Primitive
description: The 7 dimensions of a brilliance code review, formalized as queryable rules. Each dimension defines what to check, how to check it, and what constitutes a violation.

naming.question: Does the name reveal intent without requiring a comment?
checks: Name reveals intent without comment
Consistent with vocabulary already used in the codebase
Units in name where applicable (timeout_ms, buffer_bytes)
No abbreviations not universally understood in this domain

shape.question: Is the code shaped for readability and single responsibility?
checks: Single responsibility — one thing per function
No surprises — function name matches behavior
Shallow nesting — early returns/guards over if-else ladders
Function under ~40 lines (unless domain genuinely demands more)
Arguments ≤ 4 — more means extract a struct/config object
Structs with boolean fields that gate sibling optional fields → flag as 'missed sum type (TB-15), convert to discriminated union'
Functions accepting untyped maps (Record<string, unknown>, Any, map[string]interface{}) and performing internal key checks → flag as 'parse at boundary violation (TB-16)'

correctness.question: Are edge cases handled and invariants preserved?
checks: Empty input, null/undefined/nil, zero, negative, max value
Off-by-one errors in loops and slices
Race conditions if concurrency is involved
Resource lifecycle — every opened handle/fd/connection closed on every path

errorHandling.question: Are errors handled, not swallowed? Are messages actionable?
checks: Errors not swallowed silently — no bare catch/except: pass
Error messages are actionable — 'File not found' over 'Error 2'
Errors propagate with context — caller can decide what to do
Panics/crashes only for programmer error, never for runtime data

testing.question: Do tests prove correctness, not just the happy path?
checks: Tests catch the bug you just introduced, not just happy path
Test names describe behavior, not implementation
No tests that pass by accident (assertions on constants, mock returning assertion value)

minimalism.question: Is every line pulling its weight?
checks: No dead code, commented-out blocks, TODO without ticket
Every import used, every variable read
No unearned abstraction — one-line helper called once is noise
Deleted lines are celebrated — a deleted line can't cause a bug

consistency.question: Does this match existing patterns in the codebase?
checks: Matches existing patterns — if project uses Result<T,E>, don't introduce callbacks
Formatting matches — line width ≤ 100, no trailing whitespace
Commit message follows project convention

severityClassification.critical: Data corruption, security vulnerability, crash on valid input
severityClassification.high: Swallowed errors, race conditions, resource leaks
severityClassification.medium: Misleading names, missing edge case, excessive nesting
severityClassification.low: Style nits (only if they break consistency)
severityClassification.praise: Positive reinforcement — something already well done

processRules.groundFirst: Read the diff and surrounding code before forming opinions. Read AGENTS.md/CONTEXT.md for conventions.
processRules.dimensionTagging: Every finding must be tagged with its dimension ID (RP-NN).
processRules.concreteFix: Every non-praise finding must include a concrete diff or code suggestion.
processRules.severityOrdering: Output findings ordered by severity: critical, high, medium, low, praise.
